title: Basic consequences of properness
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a
proper morphism of schemes.
Then $f$ is separated, universally closed, of finite type,
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. In
particular, if $S$ is affine then $X$ is separated and quasi-compact.

proof.text: By the definition of properness [def-weil-proper-morphism], the morphism is separated, universally closed, and of finite type. The finite-type condition includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so $f$ is quasi-compact. Since a separated morphism is quasi-separated [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], its diagonal is quasi-compact. If $S$ is affine, then $S$ is quasi-compact, so $X=f^{-1}(S)$ is quasi-compact by quasi-compactness of $f$, and separatedness of $f$ implies that $X$ is separated by [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated].

proof_origin.place: Definition 29.41.1, tag 01W1, together with schemes.tex Section 01KH and Lemma 01K7
